post.caption: Rose gold was once called Russian gold. It was popular in Russia in the early 1800s, and it has other names too, like pink gold and red gold. Rose gold is gold mixed with copper, and sometimes some silver. 18 karat rose gold is 75 percent pure gold, and copper and a little silver make up the rest. The jeweler Fabergé also worked with rose gold. In the 1920s, it became fashionable in the United States. Most sources call it more durable than yellow gold, karat for karat. Its color runs through the metal, so it is not plated. The more copper in the mix, the redder the gold.
